The resulting prolarvae emerge at a remarkably small size, with the estimated wet weight at birth being just 0.00032 grams [Wwb = 0.00032 grams]. In practical terms, reaching these dimensions likely requires several decades of growth in undisturbed habitats, which renders the species particularly vulnerable to fishing pressure that selectively removes the larger, older individuals from the population.

This iteroparous strategy allows individuals to buffer against interannual variability in environmental conditions and prey availability, thereby enhancing the probability of recruitment success in any given year.
